name: MCP Gateway
description: Share your workspace's tools with any AI agent, and reach tools from other workspaces in return. Install MCP Gateway and every tool your other apps expose becomes instantly callable — no per-app setup. Connect it to another gateway to pull in that workspace's tools too, with per-connection access tokens you control.

auto_start.title: Auto-start
auto_start.description: Start the MCP Gateway container when the workspace starts.

auth_required.title: Authentication required
auth_required.description: Require workspace authentication for the gateway admin and MCP endpoints. Turning this off does not disable auth entirely — your identity still gets forwarded when you're logged in, but a caller without one is now let through for the gateway's own bearer-token check to decide, instead of being blocked at this layer. Turn off to allow external bearer-token-only callers (combine with Public).

public.title: Public
public.description: Expose the gateway through the workspace public routing layer.

warm_redis_url.title: Warm-token Redis URL
warm_redis_url.description: OPTIONAL — derived automatically by probing for the same Redis agents-platform-multitenant uses for its X-Aw-Warm-Token → current-run-id mapping. Set this only to override the automatic discovery (e.g. a Redis that needs a password, or one that isn't reachable on a docker bridge gateway). If you do set it, it must point at the SAME Redis AP-MT uses (its AP_REDIS_URL/AGENTS_REDIS_URL, checking the db index matches) — AW_REDIS_URL elsewhere in this deployment is on a DIFFERENT db and will not work here. Check this workspace's mcp-gateway /healthz for whether resolution is currently config/env/probed/none.
